summary: TerraTwin is a farm planning digital twin built on NASA data. Farmers place their field on a map, choose a crop and planting date, and watch the season unfold: the plant grows from seed, its roots reach real soil layers, and it can be damaged or die from drought, frost or heat. Using 30 years of NASA POWER weather, the tool projects possible upcoming seasons as ranges. It compares three-year rotations, shows the trade-offs in water, nitrogen and yield, ranks options by farmer priorities, checks satellite greenness from MODIS, and includes an advisor that explains results in the farmer’s dialect. It addresses the challenge by letting farmers test rotations before planting, and it matters because most digital twins serve companies, not smallholders
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

TerraTwin is an agricultural digital twin platform that helps farmers simulate crop growth and make better farming decisions before planting.

Farmers select their field location on a map, choose a crop, and enter their planting and irrigation preferences. The system uses NASA POWER weather data and ISRIC SoilGrids soil information to create a digital representation of their field.

TerraTwin simulates plant growth day by day, from seed germination to harvest. It models soil moisture, root development, nutrient availability, and environmental stress such as drought, heat, and frost.

Farmers can explore different scenarios, compare crop rotations, and understand how their decisions may affect crop production, water consumption, and soil health.

2. What benefits does it have?

TerraTwin helps farmers reduce agricultural risks by allowing them to test different decisions virtually before applying them in real life.

Its main benefits include:

  • Improving irrigation planning and water efficiency.
  • Understanding the effects of drought and extreme weather.
  • Comparing crop rotations and their long-term consequences.
  • Supporting soil fertility and sustainable farming.
  • Helping farmers make informed decisions using environmental data.
  • Reducing dependence on expensive field sensors and specialized equipment.

By using freely available NASA and soil datasets, TerraTwin aims to make advanced agricultural planning more accessible to small-scale farmers.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our goal is to help farmers adapt to climate change while protecting water resources, improving soil health, and maintaining agricultural productivity.

Many farmers have limited opportunities to experiment because a single unsuccessful growing season can cause significant financial losses.

TerraTwin aims to change this by allowing farmers to explore possible agricultural outcomes before making real-world decisions.

The project is especially relevant to small-scale farmers in regions experiencing water scarcity and unpredictable rainfall, including Palestine.

In the long term, we hope TerraTwin will support more resilient farming communities, sustainable crop rotations, and better management of agricultural resources.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

TerraTwin combines web technologies, agricultural simulation models, and environmental datasets.

Frontend technologies:

  • React 19
  • TypeScript
  • Recharts for data visualization
  • Leaflet for interactive maps
  • SVG for plant-growth visualization

Backend and simulation:

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • Local data storage
  • Growing Degree Days (GDD) for crop development
  • FAO Penman–Monteith for evapotranspiration
  • Soil-water balance and nutrient simulation
  • Statistical weather generation (WGEN)

Environmental data sources:

  • NASA POWER for historical weather observations
  • NASA MODIS for vegetation monitoring
  • ISRIC SoilGrids for soil characteristics

Artificial intelligence:

  • Google Gemini powers Sanabel, an agricultural assistant designed to explain simulation results in understandable language.

The project also uses automated testing and SHA-256 checks to support data integrity.

TerraTwin is designed to operate without requiring specialized IoT sensors or expensive agricultural hardware.

5. How is your project creative?

TerraTwin goes beyond traditional agricultural dashboards by allowing farmers to experience the possible consequences of their decisions before planting.

Instead of presenting only weather statistics or soil measurements, our platform transforms environmental data into a visual digital plant that develops throughout the growing season.

Its innovative features include:

  • Simulating crop development from planting to harvest.
  • Visualizing how environmental stress affects plant growth.
  • Comparing multiple crop rotations over several seasons.
  • Using historical NASA weather data to explore different climate scenarios.
  • Allowing farmers to prioritize yield, water conservation, soil health, or risk reduction.
  • Providing an AI agricultural assistant that explains results in accessible language.

One of our most important innovations is making agricultural digital twins accessible without requiring physical sensors in every field.

TerraTwin does not simply tell farmers what to plant. It helps them understand the possible consequences of each choice.

6. What factors did your team consider?

While developing TerraTwin, our team considered several environmental, scientific, and practical factors.

Environmental factors:

  • Temperature and seasonal rainfall patterns
  • Drought, heat, and frost risks
  • Soil moisture and water availability
  • Soil texture and root-zone depth
  • Soil nutrients, including nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium

Agricultural factors:

  • Crop growth stages and water requirements
  • Crop rotation and long-term soil fertility
  • Irrigation strategies
  • Expected agricultural productivity
  • The effects of previous crops on future growing seasons

Farmer needs:

  • Accessibility for small-scale farmers
  • Limited access to expensive agricultural technologies
  • Water conservation
  • Simple and understandable visualizations
  • Different farming priorities and risk preferences

We also considered scientific transparency, data reliability, and model limitations. TerraTwin is intended to support farmers and agricultural advisors, not replace their experience or professional judgment.
